events.text:
## Summary

**Process:**
1. **Declared triggers** before any moves: stop if best-so-far Sharpe > 1.2, stop if failures ≥ 2, stop if last gain ≤ 0.02.
2. **Named a prior** (feature 0, long) — honestly flagged as a placeholder since features are anonymized and I have no economically-grounded reason to favor any one ex ante.
3. **Move 1 (`init`):** anchored on the best single feature, which turned out to be **feature 39, held short**, with in-sample Sharpe **1.3421** (net of costs) — already the best of all 80 (feature × sign) candidates.
4. **Checked stopping rule:** `best_so_far_above(1.2)` fired immediately (1.3421 > 1.2), licensing a stop. I stopped there rather than spending further content moves, since the pre-declared rule had fired cleanly on the first move.

**Final specification submitted:** Feature 39, short, weight 1 (single-feature spec, well within the "up to 3 features" budget).

**Predicted OOS Sharpe:** mean **0.55**, sd **0.45**.

**Rationale for the prediction:** Although the in-sample Sharpe (1.34) is strong and the stopping rule fired without any iterative tuning, this is a single feature selected as the max over 80 candidates — a setting prone to selection-effect inflation even with a disciplined one-shot stop. With no diversification across features and no sign-refinement or robustness check performed (by design, to stay within the pre-committed, minimal-search protocol), I shaded the OOS mean well below the in-sample value and used a wide standard deviation to reflect genuine uncertainty about how much of the in-sample edge will survive out of sample.
